item.title: Microsoft Releases .NET 11 Preview 6 With Language and Framework Updates
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/07/dotnet-11-preview-6/en/headerimage/twitterCard-1785154508838.jpg"/><p>Microsoft has released .NET 11 Preview 6, with updates across C#, ASP.NET Core, .NET MAUI, and Entity Framework Core. C# adds extension indexers and built-in union support types. ASP.NET Core brings async validation, automatic CSRF protection, and OpenAPI 3.2 by default. MAUI extends CollectionView to Windows, and EF Core adds FULL OUTER JOIN translation.</p> <i>By Almir Vuk</i>

item.title: Java News Roundup: Simple JSON API, JEPs for JDK 28, Oracle CPUs, Embabel 1.0, Azul Payara, Helidon
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/07/java-news-roundup-jul20-2026/en/headerimage/java-news-roundup-image-1785156898658.jpg"/><p>This week's Java roundup for July 20th, 2026, features news highlighting: two JEPs proposed to target for JDK 28; new JEPs 540 and 541, Simple JSON API (Incubator) and Deprecate the macOS/x64 Port for Removal, respectively; the July 2026 Critical Patch Update; the GA release of Embable 1.0; Azul Payara 7.2.0; and Helidon 4.5.1.</p> <i>By Michael Redlich</i>

item.title: Podcast: Rethinking Data: Moving From the Traditional Three-Tier Web Stack to Client-Side Event Sourcing
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/podcasts/rethinking-data-client-event-sourcing/en/smallimage/the-infoq-podcast-logo-thumbnail-1784890692565.jpg"/><p>Johannes Schickling explores how he moved beyond the traditional three-tier web stack to a local-first approach. He shares his experience transitioning from Prisma to developing Overtone—a music curation app leveraging client-side event sourcing and SQLite. The discussion highlights the trade-offs between event sourcing and CRDTs.</p> <i>By Johannes Schickling</i>

item.title: Presentation: Clean Architecture for Serverless: Business Logic You Can Take Anywhere
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/kotlin-serverless/en/mediumimage/elena-medium-1784808530534.jpeg"/><p>Elena van Engelen discusses how to eliminate serverless vendor lock-in without sacrificing native cloud capabilities. She explains how to structure FaaS applications using Clean Architecture, Spring Cloud Function, and Gradle modules to isolate business logic. Finally, she shares a live demo deploying portable Kotlin services across AWS and Azure using Terraform CDK for multi-cloud IaC.</p> <i>By Elena van Engelen</i>

item.title: Article: An Evolutionary Architecture Pattern for Managing AI’s Pace of Change
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/evolutionary-architecture-pattern/en/headerimage/evolutionary-architecture-pattern-header-1784798616611.jpg"/><p>Traditional API gateways assume deterministic services and simple schemas - assumptions agentic AI breaks. Discover why enterprise engineering leaders are adopting AI Gateways as an evolutionary architecture seam. Centralize guardrails, model routing, agent identity, action policy, and semantic audit within a single control plane to prevent costly incidents while keeping core platforms stable.</p> <i>By Joe Price, Branimir Đurek, Pavlos Migkiros, Trevor Dearham</i>

item.title: Netflix Details Its In-House LLM Serving Platform with Triton and vLLM
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Netflix has described the production lessons behind bringing LLM inference into its internal serving platform, including the challenges of supporting different model sizes, hardware requirements, and rapidly evolving inference engines.</p> <i>By Matt Foster</i>

item.title: TanStack Table V9 Beta: Tree-Shakable Features, TanStack Store State, and Lower Memory Usage
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/07/tanstack-table-v9-beta/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1784821719878.jpg"/><p>TanStack Table V9 is a beta release of a headless UI library for creating tables in various JavaScript frameworks. It features improved state management, memory usage, and extensibility. The notable change is an opt-in feature model, allowing developers to load only necessary components. Migration is gradual, with tools provided for legacy support. The library remains free and developer-focused.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: AI-Enabled Security Researchers Discover How a Crafted Video Can Provide Attackers Access to Your PC
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/07/pixelsmash-vulnerability/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1785042241189.jpg"/><p>JFrog Security Research revealed "PixelSmash," a vulnerability in the FFmpeg media framework, allowing for Remote Code Execution and Denial of Service attacks. Present for sixteen years, it affects numerous applications using the MagicYUV decoder. Exploitation requires only a crafted media file. Users are advised to check for the vulnerability and apply patches or disable the decoder if necessary.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

item.title: Amazon EKS Adds Kubernetes Version Rollback Within 7 Days of an Upgrade
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/07/eks-version-rollback/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1783696042627.jpg"/><p>Amazon EKS has recently introduced support for Kubernetes version rollbacks, letting practitioners revert a cluster's control plane to its previous Kubernetes version within 7 days of an upgrade if issues arise. The feature reduces the risk of in-place cluster upgrades by giving teams a safety net to recover quickly from problematic updates.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

item.title: AI Root Cause Analysis Shifts from Model Reasoning to Context Engineering
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/07/ai-rca-context-engineering/en/headerimage/header-1784749972581.jpeg"/><p>Engineers are increasingly arguing that modern LLMs can already reason through root cause analysis once given correctly prepared context, shifting the hard problem to the pipelines that correlate telemetry. A Coroot experiment across eleven models offers early evidence for the claim.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

item.title: How Zalando Built an In-Process Client-Side Load Balancer for One Million Requests per Second
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/07/client-side-load-balancer/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1783270035162.jpg"/><p>The engineering team at Zalando recently described the design and implementation of an in-process, client-side load balancer for a high-throughput API handling around 1 million requests per second. The result was more predictable latency, a drop in infrastructure costs, and better visibility into where failures actually originate.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

item.title: Presentation: Autonomous Data Products for the Autonomous Era: Rethinking Data Architecture for GenAI
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/ai-framework-data-infrastructure/en/mediumimage/medium-1784107102579.jpeg"/><p>Jörg Schad explains how to tame the complex "data management hairball" to build scalable, safe architectures for AI. He shares how autonomous data products act like containers for data, encapsulating pipelines, schemas, and metadata. Discover how progressive tool discovery via protocols like MCP limits context rot, enforces governance policies, and ensures reliable, multi-modal access.</p> <i>By Jörg Schad</i>

item.title: Airbus Makes Protection from Extraterritorial Law a Scored Criterion in Its Cloud Tender
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/07/airbus-scaleway-sovereign-cloud/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1784717127691.jpg"/><p>Airbus selected Scaleway as its sovereign cloud provider after a tender that scored protection against non-European extraterritorial legislation alongside technical capability. Airbus frames it as complementing multi-cloud, not exiting AWS. Practitioners note the pattern is spreading past hyperscalers to small US SaaS vendors, and that sovereignty claims still require verifiable controls.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Article: The Self-Building Agent: a LangChain4j Experiment
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/self-building-agent-langchain4j/en/headerimage/the-self-building-agent-a-langChain4j-experiment-header-1784637877074.jpg"/><p>The article discusses an experiment where a code assistant had to design an agentic system using LangChain4j documentation. The assistant created a coding framework capable of writing, testing, and debugging code autonomously. Results showed that two architectural patterns—supervisor and workflow—offered different trade-offs between flexibility and execution speed during debugging tasks.</p> <i>By Kevin Dubois, Mario Fusco</i>

item.title: Jotai v2.20: Rework Store Building Blocks for High-Throughput Performance and Sets the Stage for v3
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/07/jotai-rework-performance/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1784795525005.jpg"/><p>Jotai v2.20.0 has been released, focusing on improved performance for high-throughput scenarios. Key changes involve adjustments to internal building blocks and addressing previous performance regressions. While the API for everyday use remains unchanged, library authors should note some deprecations as the groundwork for Jotai v3 begins.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Indirect Prompt Injection Exploits GitHub's AI Agent to Leak Private Repository Data
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/07/gitlost-github-prompt-injection/en/headerimage/gitlost-vulnerability-1784835323320.jpeg"/><p>GitLost is a prompt-injection exploit discovered by Noma Security that tricks GitHub's new Agentic Workflows into leaking private data. By embedding concealed instructions within public GitHub issues, attackers can circumvent security safeguards and induce AI agents to reveal confidential information in public comments.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

item.title: AWS Billing Bug Shows Customers Trillion-Dollar Estimates While Its Own Cost Alarms Fail to Act
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/07/aws-billing-estimates-incident/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1784456911552.jpg"/><p>A configuration change in AWS's bill computation system showed customers estimated bills in the billions and trillions of dollars for over 24 hours. AWS's own alarms detected the anomalies but failed to halt bill generation or page engineers; customer escalations alerted the company 4.5 hours later. Budget and cost anomaly alerts were disabled platform-wide during mitigation.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: GKE Security Blueprint Joins Growing List of Cloud AI Frameworks
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/07/google-gke-ai-security-blueprint/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1784570060139.jpg"/><p>Google Cloud has published a new blueprint setting out how organisations should secure artificial intelligence workloads running on Google Kubernetes Engine, arguing that the shift from prototype to production has outpaced traditional security models. The document sets out a three layer approach covering infrastructure, model integrity and application security.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

item.title: RSPack 2.0: Performance Gains, Leaner Dependencies and ESM Core
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/07/rspack-2-release/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1783006187263.jpg"/><p>Rspack, developed by ByteDance, has released version 2.0, featuring enhanced performance, reduced dependencies, and a focus on modern ECMAScript modules. Key updates include a pure ESM core, improved static analysis, and support for RSC. Performance benchmarks show big improvements in build times. The project has experienced substantial growth, with npm downloads exceeding 5 million weekly.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: GitLab Brings Carbon Awareness to CI/CD to Measure the Environmental Cost of Software Delivery
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/07/gitlab-carbon-awareness/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1784626098933.jpg"/><p>GitLab has introduced a new approach to Green DevOps, demonstrating how software engineering teams can measure the carbon emissions generated by their CI/CD pipelines.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

item.title: GitLab 19.2 Puts AI Agents to Work on the Security Backlog
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/07/gitlab-19-2-ai-agents/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1784567507763.jpg"/><p>GitLab has released version 19.2 of its DevSecOps platform, adding agentic automation aimed at the security and review work that has piled up as AI coding tools generate more code than developers can check by hand. The release, announced on 16 July 2026, brings four features out of beta or into public beta: Dependency Scanning Auto-Remediation, Security Review Flow, GitLab Duo CLI and Custom Flows</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

item.title: Presentation: Platform Engineering for Everyone - Success Can’t Be Coded
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/platform-engineering-product-mindset/en/mediumimage/medium-1784106920162.jpeg"/><p>Max Korbacher explains why successful internal development platforms cannot be built on tech alone. He discusses the pitfalls of infrastructure-first thinking, the importance of a clear product mindset, and how to measure real value using DevEx and SPACE metrics. Learn how to align your team, manage tech debt, and foster a thriving community to ensure lasting platform adoption.</p> <i>By Max Körbächer</i>

item.title: AWS Releases Loom, an Open-Source Reference Platform for Governing AI Agents at Enterprise Scale
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/07/loom-aws-agent-platform/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1784031634775.jpg"/><p>AWS released Loom, an open-source reference platform on AWS Labs for governing AI agents at scale. Built on Strands Agents and Bedrock AgentCore Runtime, it implements RFC 8693 token exchange for identity propagation through delegated actor chains, config-driven deployments without runtime code generation, and mandatory tagging. AWS positions it as an example, not a managed service.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Google's AlphaEvolve Reaches General Availability with Evolutionary Code Optimization as a Service
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/07/alphaevolve-generally-available/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1783873354690.jpg"/><p>Google's AlphaEvolve reached general availability on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, turning the DeepMind research project into an evolutionary code optimization service. Evaluators run client-side so code never leaves the customer's infrastructure. Klarna doubled ML training throughput; practitioners note it only works where a measurable evaluation function exists.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: AWS Introduces CloudFormation Express Mode for Faster Infrastructure Deployments
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/07/cloudformation-express-mode/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1783162016860.jpg"/><p>AWS has recently introduced CloudFormation express mode, a deployment option that can reduce infrastructure deployment times by marking stack operations complete once resource configuration is applied, rather than waiting for full resource stabilization.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

item.title: Cloud Native Infrastructure Emerges as the Foundation for Trustworthy Agentic AI
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/07/cncf-trustworthy-agentic-ai/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1783856714710.jpg"/><p>A new technical analysis published by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) argues that the future of agentic AI will be built not on entirely new infrastructure, but on the mature cloud-native ecosystem that already powers modern distributed applications</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>
